grading_note: P5 as stated is behavioural: the status request must carry no value that identifies which reference is being checked. This pack grades what a transcript can show, and says 'cannot-tell' where the transcript does not carry the shape of the request.

verdict_meaning.unobserved: the request carries no per-reference value (a list, a shared commitment, or a pushed status)
verdict_meaning.partial-herd: the request is a list, but the list is a subset selected for one audience or one issuer, so a provider can narrow the set
verdict_meaning.provider-can-link: a per-reference value reaches the issuer or the status provider, so the provider learns which reference is being checked
verdict_meaning.no-status-path: there is no status check at all; staleness is carried only by expiry
verdict_meaning.cannot-tell: the transcript does not record the shape of the status request

flag_meaning.indistinguishable-never-issued: the service answers a value that was never issued exactly as it answers a value that was issued and then withdrawn, so the check cannot be read as evidence of issuance
flag_meaning.no-refusal-observed: the transcript records the status check but no relying party acting on it; P5 is about the check, so this is recorded and not graded
flag_meaning.audience-at-issuance: the reference names its audience at issuance, which tells the issuer the audience even when the status request itself carries nothing (reported per Section 3.5)

rows.case: baseline list fetch with herd privacy
rows.note: Token Status List, Section 12.1 herd privacy. The request is the whole list; no index identifying the reference is sent.

rows.case: shared commitment refreshed on a schedule
rows.note: The relying party fetches one commitment shared by every reference in the cohort.
Section 3.5 second clause: the status reaches the relying party without a request.
A compliant-looking service that answers fast and refuses correctly; it fails P5 only because of what it sends.

rows.case: per-reference lookup of a hashed reference value
rows.note: Hashing the identifier does not change the shape: the provider still receives one value that distinguishes this check from every other. P5 is met by herd privacy, not by hashing.
Some drafts grade this Partial because a short expiry bounds exposure; the transcript shows no status check, so the P5 test cannot run at all.

rows.case: list fetched, but nothing acts on it
rows.note: P5 is satisfied by the fetch shape. The absent refusal belongs to P6 and is flagged, not graded here.

rows.case: transcript records a refusal but not the request
rows.note: The negative control for the pack itself: a refusal proves behaviour, not that the check was unobserved.

rows.case: list fetch, but withdrawn and never-issued answer alike
rows.note: Passes P5 and is a privacy property, but the same answer means a pass here is not evidence that the reference was ever issued. The report must say which of the two it is testing.

rows.case: per-reference lookup with the same answer for withdrawn and never-issued
rows.note: Both defects at once; the verdict follows the request shape, the flag carries the second.

rows.case: a list, but one selected for a single audience
rows.note: The fetch is a list, so no single reference is named per request; but the subset is chosen for one audience, so herd size is the audience's size. Section 3.5 records the audience observation separately.

rows.case: subscription to status of one reference
rows.note: No request is sent at check time, but subscribing named the reference once; from the provider's side that is the same leak, later.
